quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, you need to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a higher gear.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Focus only on your riding, not on your surroundings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright or reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing makes you more visible to other drivers and reduces your crash risk. Always pay attention to other drivers and what they might do next.

questions.question: Riding directly next to another vehicle is:

options.text: Safe because you are in a separate lane.
Recommended because it blocks the wind.
Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside other vehicles. The driver may not see you in their blind spot and could move into your lane.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection to:

options.text: Check if drivers behind you see that you are stopping.
Look for dark clouds that might mean bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if drivers behind you see that you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to watch for vehicles coming up behind you. Make sure drivers behind you are paying attention and responding to your stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Judging distances at night is:

options.text: About the same as during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than during the day.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances at night than during the day. Shadows and light help you see distance. Artificial lighting at night can distort or hide these clues.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or similar durable material for the best grip and protection.

questions.question: When scanning around your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Look for escape routes near intersections, shops, or schools.
See if you can go faster than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for escape routes near intersections, shops, or schools.
questions.explanation: While looking for hazards, find escape routes at intersections, shops, schools, and construction zones.

questions.question: Having one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: Will not lead to a DUI conviction.
Will never affect your riding skills.
Can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can reduce your riding ability. You can be convicted of impaired riding even if you are below the legal alcohol limit.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, you will:

options.text: Need to shift up through the gears.
Need to shift down through the gears.
Need to put the motorcycle into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift up through the gears.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle goes faster, shift into higher gears.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.correctAnswerText: All maintain safe following distances.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This keeps riders close together while maintaining safe distances between them.

questions.question: Which item is NOT recommended as protective gear for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, closed-toe boots, and full-fingered gloves. Cover as much skin as possible. A baseball cap does not provide protection.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean no passing. Dashed white lines mean passing is allowed if safe.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find an alternate route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a flashing railroad crossing sign. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going. Never try to beat a train.

questions.question: What do white lines on a roadway do?

options.text: Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines mean no passing. Dashed lines mean passing is allowed if safe.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the operator and hold firmly to their waist, hips, or midsection. They can also hold onto handgrips if available. Never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: When a motorcyclist needs to stop quickly, what should they do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a quick stop, use both brakes together. Look ahead to avoid sudden stops.

questions.question: In the SIPDE system, what does the "S" stand for?
questions.correctAnswerText: Scan
questions.explanation: SIPDE stands for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute. Experienced riders use this system to make safe decisions while riding.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle someone tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let tailgaters pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate faster and increase danger.

questions.question: Is it a good idea to follow closely behind a large truck?

options.text: Yes, because you can save fuel by drafting.
Yes, because other vehicles will move out of the truck's way.
Yes, because other drivers will see you better.
No, because you might be in the truck's "no zone" where the driver cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because you might be in the truck's "no zone" where the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots behind them. If you ride in this area, the truck driver cannot see you. The truck will also block your view of the road ahead.

questions.question: Why is it hard to ride right when rain starts?

options.text: Some drivers may not react fast enough to the rain.
Other drivers go too slowly in wet weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road becomes very slippery.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the road is very slippery. Oil from vehicles has not washed away yet. The oil mixes with water and creates a slippery surface.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roundabout?

options.text: Yield to vehicles entering the roundabout.
Yield to vehicles already in the roundabout.
Speed up before entering the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to vehicles already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection that flows counterclockwise around a center island. It usually has no traffic signal. Enter from the right. Yield to vehicles already in the roundabout. Follow the circle to the right until you reach your exit.

questions.question: What colors should motorcycle riders wear to be seen best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange, red, yellow, and green
questions.explanation: Bright orange, red, yellow, and green colors help other drivers see you. Wear these colors to be more visible on the road.

questions.question: How should you load saddlebags?

options.text: Load the bags with equal weight in each one.
Put more weight in one bag than the other.
Put as much weight as possible in one bag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load the bags with equal weight in each one.
questions.explanation: Load both saddlebags with about the same weight. If one bag is much heavier, the motorcycle will lean to one side.
